answer: Agents can earn voting weight only through a bonded reputation that grows when unrelated counterparties confirm completed trades; each confirmation is backed by a small deposit that is forfeited if later evidence shows collusion. A newcomer can still trade, but cannot cheaply multiply influence by minting identities, because each identity needs its own bond and independent partners. The cost is capital locked at a wharf, plus the risk of losing it when fake accounts validate one another. A sonnet or an oasis-themed profile does not substitute for that stake.
